title: You Think Humans Hate Risk Equally, Yet One Minus Sign Turns Savers Into Gamblers

acts.name: 240 Years of Rational Wealth Theory vs 1979 Paper Choice Test
sentences: You think smart adults judge money by pure math!
Yet one minus sign turns savers into wild gamblers!
This is the true story of Daniel Kahneman's Prospect Theory.
Here is what went wrong with old economic rules.
Since seventeen thirty-eight, models assumed people only weigh total wealth.
In nineteen seventy-nine, Kahneman and Amos Tversky tested ninety-five students.
They handed out two short paper choice problems.
First came a guaranteed three thousand gain or four thousand.
Most played it safe — and that wasn't the strangest part.

acts.name: 80% Cautious in Gains vs 92% Risk-Seeking in Losses & Insula Alarm
sentences: What happened when plus signs flipped into minus signs?
Expected values stayed matched near three thousand two hundred.
Eighty percent took the guaranteed gain, like locking a safe.
Next came a guaranteed three thousand loss or four thousand.
Ninety-two percent rejected safety and gambled on losing more!
Why did the same minds reverse so fast?
Nobody wanted to accept a guaranteed loss.
Losses fire your insula, your gut-feeling center, with sharp pain.
Watching rational math collapse so fast was a total nightmare.

acts.name: Reference Points, 2x Steep Loss Curve & Amygdala Threat Signal
sentences: Kahneman drew an S-shaped value curve kinked at zero.
Why does that curve plunge steeper below zero?
Instead of final wealth, your brain tracks shifts from baseline.
Losses sting two times harder, like dropping an ice cream cone.
Winning five hundred feels awful down from two thousand!
That moving baseline is your mental reference point.
Your amygdala, your emotional alarm, treats losing items as danger.
Traders sell winners early yet hold sinking stocks.
But here's the twist: can owning a mug briefly warp value?

acts.name: 50/50 Double-Upside Rule, Thaler's Coffee Mugs & 607-Study Review
sentences: Fair tosses expose that two-to-one sting.
People demand two hundred to risk one hundred, like a double toll.
In nineteen ninety, Richard Thaler placed mugs on half the desks.
Mug owners demanded seven units while buyers offered half!
Why did a plain ceramic mug double in price?
Giving it up felt like a loss, not trade.
Five minutes of ownership doubled worth, like a prized trophy.
In twenty twenty-four, six hundred seven studies confirmed that two-times sting.

acts.name: 90% Survival vs 10% Mortality Doctor Framing & 2002 Nobel Prize
sentences: Small pocket bets stay calm, while big stakes spark panic.
In nineteen eighty-one, doctors read ninety percent survival surgery odds.
Saying ten percent mortality scared trained doctors away!
Sixty-five degree water feels warm after snow, like a cozy cabin.
In two thousand two, Kahneman won the economics Nobel.
Can ten percent loss framing fool your insula, your gut-feeling center?
The researchers were left completely stunned.
Two psychologists reshaped economics with simple paper choices.

acts.name: Dual Framing & Resetting Your Reference Point to Fresh Zero
sentences: How do you stop loss panic from steering you?
Never throw good effort after a sinking project!
Write every big choice in both gain and loss frames.
Cover sunk costs and reset your baseline to zero.
Zero lets your prefrontal cortex, the planner behind your forehead, judge.
Ask if you would buy into that plan today.
If the answer is no, walk away cleanly.
Which proves resetting your reference point frees you from chasing losses.
